title: Derived pullback of modules on schemes
statement:
Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with ring map $g^\sharp:g^{-1}\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_T$, and let $D(\mathcal O_S)$, $D(\mathcal O_T)$ be the derived categories of [def-pc-derived-category]. The *derived pullback* $Lg^*:D(\mathcal O_S)\to D(\mathcal O_T)$ is the composite of the termwise inverse image $g^{-1}:D(\mathcal O_S)\to D(g^{-1}\mathcal O_S)$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (well defined because $g^{-1}$ is exact) with the derived change of rings along $g^\sharp$ on the site of open subsets of $T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]:

$$
Lg^*E=\mathcal O_T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_S}g^{-1}E.
$$

It is computed by a K-flat resolution: for every K-flat resolution $\mathcal P^\bullet\to E$ of a complex of $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] (one exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]), $g^{-1}\mathcal P^\bullet\to g^{-1}E$ is a K-flat resolution over $g^{-1}\mathcal O_S$, and $Lg^*E\cong g^*\mathcal P^\bullet=\mathcal O_T\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_S}g^{-1}\mathcal P^\bullet$, the termwise module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] (sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], as a complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]), canonically in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ and independently of the resolution.

proof.text: Obtain the additive exact inverse-image functor I and its K-flat resolution clause from the inverse-image preservation theorem.

Take E to be the recorded tensor pullback. Its adjunction with pushforward makes it a left adjoint, so it preserves finite colimits and is additive. Its induced homotopy functor is triangulated by the additive mapping-cone construction, and so is its composite F with the target derived localization.

Let C consist of homotopy-category objects represented by K-flat complexes. Every homotopy object is represented by a complex G. Choose a K-flat resolution P -> G; quotienting gives a quasi-isomorphism from an object of C. For any morphism between two objects of C, fullness of the homotopy quotient gives a representative complex map. If it is a quasi-isomorphism, tensor pullback preserves that property by the preservation theorem; the target derived localization therefore inverts it.

Apply the resolving-class left-derived theorem to F and C. It supplies L, the universal counit, a shift-compatible triangulated structure, and a counit isomorphism on C. Every K-flat complex P represents an object of C, giving the required final clause. Combine these with I and the definitional object and map formulas for E.
